en: Abhidhānottaratantra, Chapter 25 [Tibetan & Sanskrit, 28] = Lokesh Chandra facsimile edition = 1138 AD palm-leaf manuscript.
[107] One should visualize Utpala and Akuśa as the embodiment of primordial wisdom;
one should visualize the triad of body, speech, and mind in the center of the wheel.
Just as it is for Vajrasattva through the previously described application of the seats,
so too should one recollect the mantra born from the secret of Mañjuvajra,
which is the commitment of the wisdom of the three secrets, conjoined with the heroes and yoginīs.
Oṃ śrīmahāsukhamañjuvajra āḥ maṃ hūṃ ḍākinījālasamvara svāhā.
Having well-restrained the breath through *prāṇāyāma*, the observer of the great vow (*mahāvratī*) should recite the mantra.
He should emanate the secret wheel and withdraw the triple world.
This supreme secret must not be told to just anyone.
The twenty-fifth chapter, the Mañjuvajra-sādhana, from the *Abhidhānottarottara*.
